actions.name: Derive a Cosmos multisig account
actions.summary: The room agrees on a threshold k and an ordered list of n member keys, and each member confirms their own key. The address is a hash of that policy. Nothing goes on chain now: the account appears when it first receives funds, and its keys become public on its first signed transaction.

fields.name: threshold
fields.means: k: how many of the listed keys must sign (1 to n)

fields.name: keys
fields.means: the n member public keys (secp256k1 by default), in the order they are hashed

fields.name: order
fields.means: sorted by each key's address (what keys add --multisig does) or as given (--nosort); the order changes the address

fields.name: chain
fields.means: the chain the account is for: CAIP-2 cosmos:<chain_id>, and its bech32 address prefix

fields.name: address
fields.means: the derived address: the first 20 bytes of SHA-256 over the amino encoding of LegacyAminoPubKey{threshold, pubkeys}

agreement.threshold: n of n: every listed key holder confirms their own key; nothing is signed on chain

steps.does: Names k, the member keys and their order. Muster would build LegacyAminoPubKey{threshold, pubkeys} and hash its amino bytes (route tendermint/PubKeyMultisigThreshold): the address is the first 20 bytes of SHA-256. The same keys in another order, or another k, give another address. The chain accepts any keys here; it asks for no proof that their holders agreed.

Each member re-derives the address from k and the ordered keys, and confirms that the key listed for them is theirs. A member confirms only their own key. The client reads the chain's TxSigLimit from the x/auth params through the user's RPC and records the read.

The room records the account: address, k and the ordered keys. The chain has nothing yet. x/bank creates the account when it first receives coins, with an account number and no public key. The keys and k stay off chain until the account first signs: that transaction must carry the whole LegacyAminoPubKey, which x/auth checks against the address and then stores on the account.

refusals.what: an account disclosure whose address does not re-derive from its k and its ordered keys
refusals.why: invariant 1: re-derive or refuse. The address is a hash over the ordered amino bytes, so the same keys in another order are another account

refusals.what: a policy whose key count (nested multisig keys counted) exceeds the chain's TxSigLimit, read and recorded (default 7)
refusals.why: the chain's rule: ValidateSigCountDecorator counts every key in the multisig, signed or not, and rejects the transaction. Such an account could receive coins and never spend them

refusals.what: presenting a listed key as a member's before that member has confirmed it in the room
refusals.why: invariant 9: the client says about a member only what that member disclosed. The chain takes any keys with no proof of possession; a key nobody confirms is shown as a signer outside the room

refusals.what: a policy that lists the same key more than once, unless the room is shown that its holder counts more than once
refusals.why: the chain's rule allows repeated keys; the holder then supplies several of the k signatures, so k of n would not mean k people

refusals.what: a threshold below 1 or above n
refusals.why: the chain's constructor rejects it (NewLegacyAminoPubKey panics on k <= 0 or n < k)

claims.claim: The address commits to k and to every key, in order. Change any of them and the address changes.
Until the account first signs, the chain holds no public key for it: an observer sees only an address and its balance.
On the account's first signed transaction, anyone reading the chain learns all n keys and k, and they stay in state.
The chain does not check that a listed key's holder agreed to join the account.
claims.party: a proposer who lists a key its holder does not control

claims.claim: On default parameters a multisig with more than 7 keys (say 3 of 8) can never spend: TxSigLimit counts all n keys.

evidence.what: LegacyAminoPubKey: constructor (k in 1..n, repeated keys allowed), Address() = AddressHash of the amino bytes, key order preserved
the amino codec for the multisig key: route tendermint/PubKeyMultisigThreshold and the registered key types
LegacyAminoPubKey proto: threshold + public_keys (amino field name pubkeys, threshold written as a string)
CometBFT SumTruncated: SHA-256, first 20 bytes
CometBFT AddressHash = tmhash.SumTruncated
keys add --multisig: keys sorted by address unless --nosort; duplicate key names rejected
SetPubKeyDecorator stores the multisig key on first spend and checks it hashes to the signer address; ValidateSigCountDecorator counts all subkeys against TxSigLimit
x/auth DefaultTxSigLimit = 7
x/bank creates the recipient account if it does not exist
SignerInfo.public_key is optional only for accounts that already have a key in state
cosmos-sdk v0.55.0 CHANGELOG: ML-DSA-65 keys with multisig support (#26436, #26472)

unverified: Which key types a given chain accepts inside a multisig for transaction signing (the registry lists secp256k1-ecdsa, ed25519 and ml-dsa-65; v0.55 registers ed25519, secp256k1, bls12_381, ML-DSA-65 and secp256k1eth in the multisig codec). Only secp256k1 is described here.
Where each chain's bech32 prefix and a non-default TxSigLimit are read from in practice (chain registry vs node params) was not checked per chain.

actions.name: Send coins from a Cosmos multisig
actions.summary: k of the n key holders send coins from the multisig with a bank MsgSend. Each signs the same amino-JSON sign doc; one member assembles the multisignature and broadcasts. The x/auth ante handler on the chain checks the threshold.

fields.name: from
fields.means: the multisig account's address: the MsgSend from_address and the fee payer

fields.name: to
fields.means: the payee's address

fields.name: amount
fields.means: the coins to send: a list of {denom, amount}

fields.name: fee
fields.means: the fee coins and the gas limit; the multisig pays (it is the first and only signer)

fields.name: memo
fields.means: the transaction memo; public once broadcast

fields.name: timeout_height
fields.means: optional: the last block height at which the transaction is valid; 0 means none

fields.name: chain_id
fields.means: the chain id every signature commits to

fields.name: account_number
fields.means: the multisig's account number, read from the chain

fields.name: sequence
fields.means: the multisig's sequence, read from the chain at propose; the transaction is valid only at this sequence

agreement.threshold: k of n keys (the multisig's LegacyAminoPubKey threshold)

steps.does: Composes MsgSend{from_address: the multisig, to_address, amount}, the fee (coins and gas limit), the memo and an optional timeout_height, as tx bank send --generate-only would. Muster would read the multisig's account_number and sequence through the user's RPC and record both reads. Every room member re-derives the same sign doc. The RPC provider learns which account is being prepared.

Each key holder re-derives the sign doc and signs it with their own key, as tx sign --multisig=<address> --sign-mode amino-json does. A contribution is the member's public key, sign mode, signature and sequence: the signature file tx multisign reads.
steps.signs: SHA-256 of the SIGN_MODE_LEGACY_AMINO_JSON sign doc, signed with the member's own secp256k1 key (ECDSA; a 64-byte r||s signature in low-S form). The sign doc is compact JSON with keys sorted at every level: {account_number, chain_id, fee: {amount: [{amount, denom}], gas[, granter][, payer]}, memo, msgs: [{type: cosmos-sdk/MsgSend, value: {amount: [{amount, denom}], from_address, to_address}}], sequence[, timeout_height][, timeout_timestamp][, unordered]}. Every uint64 is a decimal string. The bracketed fields are left out when empty or zero. account_number and sequence are the multisig account's, not the member's. chain_id is inside the bytes (explicit binding); so are the fee, the memo and the expiry. Not inside: any public key, the multisig policy, which other keys sign, or their signatures, so each member signs without knowing who else will.

steps.does: Once k signatures verify, any member assembles the transaction, as tx multisign does. The multisignature is a CompactBitArray of n bits marking which keys signed, in the multisig's key order, plus the signatures in that same order. The signer info carries the LegacyAminoPubKey (all n keys and k), ModeInfo.Multi with LEGACY_AMINO_JSON for each signer, and the sequence. The member broadcasts it through their own RPC. The RPC provider sees the signed transaction first. Validators and the mempool see it next, before inclusion. The chain's ante handler checks that all n keys fit TxSigLimit, that the sequence is the account's current one, that at least k bits are set, and that each signature verifies. It charges verification gas for every signature present, and deducts the fee from the multisig.

The client watches for the block that includes the transaction. CometBFT commits a block when more than 2/3 of validator voting power precommits it. The fee and the sequence are spent in the ante handler, whose writes are kept even if the message itself then fails. On the account's first spend, x/auth stores the multisig public key on the account, so it stays readable in state.

refusals.what: a contribution whose signature does not verify over the sign doc muster re-derived, or that was made in any sign mode but LEGACY_AMINO_JSON
refusals.why: invariant 1 (F-4): re-derive, refuse on mismatch. tx multisign supports only amino-json; SIGN_MODE_DIRECT is not supported for a multisig

refusals.what: assembling or broadcasting once the multisig's sequence has moved past the one in the sign doc
refusals.why: the chain's rule: a signature whose sequence is not the account's current sequence fails (ErrWrongSequence). Any other transaction from the multisig first voids every signature collected at the old sequence

refusals.what: signing when account_number, sequence or chain_id reached the sign doc without a recorded read
refusals.why: invariant 10: all three are chain state inside the signed bytes, read through the RPC

refusals.what: a signature from a key that is not in the multisig's key list
refusals.why: the chain's rule: a signature is placed by its key's index in the policy, and tx multisign refuses a key outside it

refusals.what: submitting after the proposal's timeout_height
refusals.why: invariant 2 (expiry): the chain rejects a transaction past its timeout height (ErrTxTimeoutHeight)

refusals.what: a transaction body that carries extension options
refusals.why: the amino-json sign mode refuses to produce sign bytes for such a body, so no member could sign it

refusals.what: a send from a policy whose key count exceeds the chain's TxSigLimit
refusals.why: the chain's rule: every key counts, signed or not, so the transaction is rejected whatever k signed

claims.claim: Every member signs the same bytes, and they name the chain (chain_id) and the account (account_number). A signature is worthless on another chain or for another account.
The multisig's sequence is inside the signed bytes. Any other transaction from the account first makes every collected signature stale.

The chain itself checks that k of the n keys signed. The ways around it are grants the account itself made, each signed k of n: an x/authz grant lets the grantee execute the granted message types for the account with no multisig signatures, and an x/feegrant allowance lets the grantee's transaction fees be paid from the account, up to the allowance.
claims.party: a grantee the multisig authorized through x/authz or x/feegrant

claims.claim: At settlement anyone reading the chain learns all n keys and k (first spend), which keys signed, the payee, the amount and the memo.
The RPC provider learns which account is being prepared when muster reads its account number and sequence, and sees the signed transaction before the network does.
Approving costs a member nothing directly. Each signature adds verification gas to the one fee the multisig pays.

evidence.what: MsgSend {from_address, to_address, amount}; amino name cosmos-sdk/MsgSend; signer from_address

tx sign --multisig: a member signs on behalf of the multisig account and outputs a signature only

SignerInfo (public_key optional once in state, mode_info, sequence), ModeInfo.Multi (bitarray + per-signer modes), TxBody timeout_height / unordered / timeout_timestamp

TxTimeoutHeightDecorator rejects a transaction past timeout_height or timeout_timestamp
runTx writes the ante handler's state (fee, sequence) before running messages, so they stay spent if a message fails
the fee payer is the first signer unless fee.payer is set

But tx sign --multisig and tx multisign fill in the multisig's on-chain sequence when online, so an unordered multisig transaction appears to need --offline with sequence 0, and the chain must enable unordered transactions. Not confirmed end to end.

fields.name: contract
fields.means: the contract's address

fields.name: msg
fields.means: the JSON message passed to the contract

fields.name: funds
fields.means: coins sent to the contract with the call: a list of {denom, amount}; may be empty

fields.name: code_id
fields.means: the contract's code id, read from the chain at propose

fields.name: admin

actions.name: Change the signers of a Cosmos multisig
actions.summary: x/auth cannot re-key an account, so new signers mean a new account. The room derives the new multisig, then k of the OLD keys sign a sweep of the old account's coins to the new address. Staking and other positions do not move with the sweep.

fields.name: from
fields.means: the old multisig account's address: the sweep's sender and fee payer

fields.name: new_threshold
fields.means: k for the new policy

fields.name: new_keys
fields.means: the new policy's member keys, in hashing order

fields.name: new_address
fields.means: the new account's address, derived as in derive-account

fields.name: sweep
fields.means: the coins moved: the old account's spendable balance, less the fee in the fee denom

fields.name: not_swept
fields.means: what one MsgSend does not move, listed for the room: delegations and unbonding entries, coins still locked by vesting, contract admin roles, grants the old account made

fields.name: fee
fields.means: the fee coins and the gas limit; the multisig pays (it is the first and only signer)

fields.name: memo
fields.means: the transaction memo; public once broadcast

fields.name: timeout_height
fields.means: optional: the last block height at which the transaction is valid; 0 means none

fields.name: chain_id
fields.means: the chain id every signature commits to

fields.name: account_number
fields.means: the multisig's account number, read from the chain

fields.name: sequence
fields.means: the multisig's sequence, read from the chain at propose; the transaction is valid only at this sequence

agreement.threshold: k of n keys of the OLD policy (the old account's LegacyAminoPubKey threshold)

steps.does: Runs derive-account for the new policy first; each new member confirms their own key. Muster would read the balances, the account number and the sequence, and record each read. It lists what the sweep does not move: delegations and unbonding entries, coins locked by vesting, contract admin roles (wasm MsgUpdateAdmin), grants the old account made. Each needs its own message from the old account, under the old policy.
k holders of the OLD keys each re-derive the sweep's sign doc and sign it. The new policy's keys sign nothing here. A member being removed is still an old signer and can still approve.

steps.does: Once k signatures verify, any member assembles the transaction, as tx multisign does. The multisignature is a CompactBitArray of n bits marking which keys signed, in the multisig's key order, plus the signatures in that same order. The signer info carries the LegacyAminoPubKey (all n keys and k), ModeInfo.Multi with LEGACY_AMINO_JSON for each signer, and the sequence. The member broadcasts it through their own RPC. The RPC provider sees the signed transaction first. Validators and the mempool see it next, before inclusion. The chain's ante handler checks that all n keys fit TxSigLimit, that the sequence is the account's current one, that at least k bits are set, and that each signature verifies. It charges verification gas for every signature present, and deducts the fee from the multisig. The chain sees the old policy and the new address as the payee. It does not see the new policy: that stays off chain until the new account first signs.

The coins sit at the new address; x/bank created that account if it was new. The old account still exists under the old policy: anything later sent to it can be spent by k of the old keys, a removed member's included. x/auth has no message to replace an account's public key (ADR-034 proposed one; it is still PROPOSED), so the address changes whenever the signers do.

refusals.what: a new address that does not re-derive from the new k and the new ordered keys
refusals.why: invariant 1: re-derive or refuse; a mistyped key or order sends everything to an account no one controls

refusals.what: a sweep whose amount plus fee exceeds the spendable balance read at propose
refusals.why: the chain deducts the fee in the ante handler before the MsgSend runs, and sends only unlocked coins; an overdrawn sweep fails after the fee and the sequence are spent

refusals.what: marking the signer change complete while the old account still holds coins or positions
refusals.why: invariant 7: the room's signer set changed, but the chain's did not. The old policy still controls the old address

refusals.what: a contribution whose signature does not verify over the sign doc muster re-derived, or that was made in any sign mode but LEGACY_AMINO_JSON
refusals.why: invariant 1 (F-4): re-derive, refuse on mismatch. tx multisign supports only amino-json; SIGN_MODE_DIRECT is not supported for a multisig

refusals.what: assembling or broadcasting once the multisig's sequence has moved past the one in the sign doc
refusals.why: the chain's rule: a signature whose sequence is not the account's current sequence fails (ErrWrongSequence). Any other transaction from the multisig first voids every signature collected at the old sequence

refusals.what: signing when account_number, sequence or chain_id reached the sign doc without a recorded read
refusals.why: invariant 10: all three are chain state inside the signed bytes, read through the RPC

refusals.what: a signature from a key that is not in the multisig's key list
refusals.why: the chain's rule: a signature is placed by its key's index in the policy, and tx multisign refuses a key outside it

refusals.what: submitting after the proposal's timeout_height
refusals.why: invariant 2 (expiry): the chain rejects a transaction past its timeout height (ErrTxTimeoutHeight)

refusals.what: a transaction body that carries extension options
refusals.why: the amino-json sign mode refuses to produce sign bytes for such a body, so no member could sign it

claims.claim: There is no in-place re-key: the x/auth Msg service offers only MsgUpdateParams, so new signers mean a new address and a sweep.
Until the sweep settles, k of the old keys, a removed member's included, can still spend from the old account.
claims.party: a removed member together with enough other old signers

claims.claim: Coins sent to the old address after the sweep stay under the old policy.
claims.party: the old signers, if anyone keeps paying the old address

claims.claim: Staked coins do not move with a MsgSend: they must be unbonded first, which takes the chain's unbonding period.
The chain learns the new address when the sweep lands, but not the new keys until the new account first signs.
Every member signs the same bytes, and they name the chain (chain_id) and the account (account_number). A signature is worthless on another chain or for another account.

evidence.what: the x/auth Msg service: only UpdateParams; no message changes an account's public key
ADR-034 Account Rekeying: status PROPOSED; explains that a multisig account's key cannot be updated and that bonded coins need a full unbonding to move
x/bank: sends only unlocked coins (subUnlockedCoins) and creates the recipient account if missing
wasmd MsgUpdateAdmin: a contract admin role moves only by its own message
keys add --multisig: sort by address unless --nosort
the LEGACY_AMINO_JSON handler: AminoSignDoc = account_number, timeout_height, chain_id, sequence, memo, msgs, unordered, timeout_timestamp, fee{amount, gas, payer, granter}; refuses extension options
the AminoSignDoc / AminoSignFee proto: which fields are always written and which are omitted when empty (unordered and timeout_timestamp added in 0.53)
the amino-JSON encoder: field names sorted, compact output, uint64/int64 written as quoted decimal strings
secp256k1 Sign: ECDSA over SHA-256 of the message, 64-byte R||S, low-S enforced on verify
x/auth ante: SetPubKey stores the multisig key on first spend, sequence must equal the account's, ValidateSigCount counts all n keys against TxSigLimit, verification gas per signature present
x/auth defaults: TxSigLimit 7, SigVerifyCostSecp256k1 1000, TxSizeCostPerByte 10
LegacyAminoPubKey.VerifyMultisignature: bit array size must equal n, at least k bits set, each signature verified against the key at its index
tx multisign: reads per-member signature files, verifies each, places it by key index, sets the multisig's account number and sequence from state; SIGN_MODE_DIRECT not supported
tx sign --multisig: a member signs on behalf of the multisig account and outputs a signature only
SignTxWithSignerAddress: multisigs only support LEGACY_AMINO_JSON; account number and sequence read from the multisig's state
SignerInfo (public_key optional once in state, mode_info, sequence), ModeInfo.Multi (bitarray + per-signer modes), TxBody timeout_height / unordered / timeout_timestamp
MultiSignature {signatures} and CompactBitArray
TxTimeoutHeightDecorator rejects a transaction past timeout_height or timeout_timestamp
runTx writes the ante handler's state (fee, sequence) before running messages, so they stay spent if a message fails
the fee payer is the first signer unless fee.payer is set
Cosmos SDK docs: tx multisign assumes SIGN_MODE_LEGACY_AMINO_JSON; a multisig with a SIGN_MODE_DIRECT signer is not yet possible; --generate-only
CometBFT: a block is committed when more than 2/3 of validators precommit it; safety holds while fewer than 1/3 are Byzantine
x/authz DispatchActions: a message whose signer is the granter runs on the grantee's authority when a grant exists
cosmos-sdk v0.55.0 CHANGELOG: SIGN_MODE_TEXTUAL removed (#26456); ML-DSA-65 account keys with multisig support; unordered transactions (#23708)

unverified: Chain-specific account re-keying: ADR-034's MsgChangePubKey is not in x/auth v0.55, but whether any individual Cosmos chain ships its own account re-key module was not checked. (x/staking v0.55 added rotation of validator consensus keys, which does not re-key an account.)

The full list of positions a MsgSend does not move (distribution rewards and withdraw address, authz and feegrant grants, governance deposits, IBC-held state, validator operator roles) was not checked module by module.

Unordered transactions (cosmos-sdk v0.53+) with a multisig: the amino-json sign doc does carry unordered and timeout_timestamp, and the ante handler then requires sequence 0. But tx sign --multisig and tx multisign fill in the multisig's on-chain sequence when online, so an unordered multisig transaction appears to need --offline with sequence 0, and the chain must enable unordered transactions. Not confirmed end to end.
